rabbi.reading: A Jewish reader who lands here first reads one sentence, in the site's own voice: the Jews, acting as one body, seek to kill Jesus and conspire against Paul. Every line beneath it is true to some verse, but the picture is a people defined by murder, which is the charge that was laid against Jews for centuries, and the card gives no sign that the same text calls Jesus, Paul, Esther, Mordecai and Aquila Jews, that many Jews are said to believe in Jesus, or that the book that uses the word most (Esther) is about Jews marked for destruction. He would not ask for anything to be removed; he would ask that the card say who the people are before it says what some of them did, and that it not say 'as one body' when the text itself shows them dividing.

points.point: 'Acting as one body' is the card's own claim, and the text does not make it. In John itself the Jews are split: some who had come to Mary believed in Jesus, many were deserting the leaders and believing, and a group is addressed as 'Jews who had believed Him'. In Acts a great number of Jews believed at Iconium.

The description names only the killing. The same Gospel has Jesus say 'salvation is from the Jews', has the Samaritan woman call Jesus a Jew, and has 'King of the Jews' as the title put over him. Matthew gives it at his birth and at his trial. None of that is on the card, so a reader cannot tell that Jesus and his first followers are inside the people the card describes.

'As the Gospels and Acts present them' is not the proportion of the text. In the counts given, Matthew, Mark and Luke use the word in only 5, 6 and 5 verses each; John carries 71 and Acts 79. The word is in the Hebrew and Aramaic Bible in about 80 verses, most of them Esther, where the Jews are the ones threatened with destruction and delivered. A card that opens with the Gospels and Acts lets one slice stand for the whole.

The card files being hunted (by Haman, by the astrologers) under the same 'Conflict' heading as hunting (Jesus, Paul), in the same lines, with no sign of which way each runs. A Jewish reader scanning the list sees a people permanently 'in conflict' rather than a people who are sometimes the victim and sometimes the party accused. Direction should be visible, and so should Acts 18:2, where Claudius orders all the Jews out of Rome.

Three hard verses have been used against Jews as a people, and each needs its setting beside it rather than stripped: John 8:44 is spoken in a scene whose hearers 8:31 calls 'Jews who had believed Him'; 1 Thessalonians 2:14-15 is written by a Jew (Paul, Acts 22:3) to a church that suffered from its own countrymen as the churches of Judea did; Revelation 2:9 speaks of those who 'falsely claim to be Jews', not of Jews as such. The site need not choose a reading of any of these. It does need to cite them with their addressees and not as free-standing statements about the Jews.

Statements the text makes about the Jews that are plainly favourable are absent: they were entrusted with the words of God; God's gifts and call are irrevocable and they are loved on account of the patriarchs (said in the same breath as 'enemies on your account'); the nations will take hold of a Jew's robe because God is with him. Leaving these out while keeping the conflict is the one-sided slice the owner is worried about.

The card does not say the word is also 'Judean', and that Hebrew scripture mostly says 'Israel'. A Jewish reader knows this; a general reader does not, and may take 'the Jews' in John as the same group as the Jews of Esther. That is for the word pages to make plain, without the card choosing how John uses it.

description.proposed: The people of Judah, called Jews: Mordecai, Esther and Paul are among them, and Jesus is called a Jew and King of the Jews. The text shows them marked for destruction by Haman and rejoicing at their deliverance, and divided over Jesus: many believed in him, and some sought to kill him, and later Paul.
description.why: Every clause rests on a verse: Judah and 'the Jews' together (Neh 1:2; Jer 40:11), Mordecai the Jew (Esth 2:5; 10:3), Paul 'I am a Jew' (Acts 21:39; 22:3), Esther among the people to be destroyed (Esth 7:4), Jesus called a Jew (John 4:9) and King of the Jews (Matt 2:2; 27:11), Haman's plan to destroy all the Jews (Esth 3:6) and their joy (Esth 8:16-17), many who believed (John 11:45; 12:11; Acts 14:1), the Jews who sought to kill Jesus (John 5:18; 7:1) and conspired against Paul (Acts 9:23; 23:12). It keeps the killing verses in full, drops the claim of a single acting body, and drops 'as the Gospels and Acts present them', which is the card's own framing. It takes no position on who 'the Jews' are in John.
readers_objecting_to_proposed: No one of the nine could not accept it, but three might want a word changed. The secular scholar of the Bible may say 'people of Judah' should be read as covering Judeans as well as Jews, which the word pages handle. The Lutheran and Reformed reader may note that Romans 2:28-29 gives a further sense (a Jew inwardly) that the description does not mention; the description does not deny it, and a relation can carry it. The Catholic or Orthodox reader may want 'divided' not to read as a verdict on the people; the sentence says only that some believed and some sought his death, and cites John 11:45 and 5:18.

missing.relation: Jesus is called a Jew (a Samaritan woman: 'You are a Jew') and King of the Jews
missing.why: The card shows Jesus only as the one the Jews act against. These verses say what the word is applied to him.

missing.relation: Paul says he is a Jew, born in Tarsus and raised in Jerusalem
missing.why: Paul appears on the card only as the victim of a conspiracy. In these verses he is a member of the people described.

missing.relation: Aquila, a Jew, was among those ordered out of Rome by Claudius
missing.why: Shows the Jews as the subject of a decree against them, outside the Esther story.
Contradicts the impression that the Jews acted as one body; the text itself says otherwise.

missing.relation: Salvation is from the Jews (Jesus to the Samaritan woman)
missing.why: A statement about the Jews in the same book that supplies most of the conflict lines.

missing.relation: The Jews were entrusted with the words of God; God's gifts and call are irrevocable; they are loved on account of the patriarchs
missing.why: Romans 11:28 also says 'enemies on your account'; both halves belong together or neither.

missing.relation: God was with the Jews; the nations will take hold of a Jew's robe to go with him
missing.why: The word's one appearance in the prophets points to the nations seeking out the Jew, which the card does not show.

missing.relation: Haman planned to destroy all the Jews; they celebrated deliverance, and many of the people of the land became Jews
missing.why: The card has 'persecuted by Haman' but not the plan, the reversal, or that others joined them.

missing.relation: Jews and Greeks together: no difference; one in Christ
missing.why: The text also uses the word to say who is not set apart; the card sets the Jews apart only.

missing.relation: Hard texts, each given with its addressee: 'the Jews who killed the Lord Jesus' (said by Paul, a Jew, to a church); 'those who falsely claim to be Jews' (Rev 2:9)
missing.why: The canon is not softened. The conflict list should carry these too, honestly, with who is speaking and to whom, so the card cannot be accused of hiding the verses most used against Jews.

misleading.relation: Conflict (8): 'was persecuted by Haman' and 'attacked Jesus' listed together
misleading.why: One heading runs both ways with no direction, so the Jews read as always in conflict.
misleading.fix: Split by direction: Jews as the target (Esth 3:6, 3:13; Dan 3:8; Acts 18:2) and Jews as the party acting or accused (John 5:18; Acts 9:23).

misleading.why: Drops the setting: 8:31 names the hearers 'the Jews who had believed Him', and the rebuke is Jesus speaking to Jews in a dispute. As a bare line it reads as a verdict on the people.
misleading.fix: Say who was addressed: 'Jesus tells Jews who had believed him that they want to carry out the devil's desires' (John 8:31, 8:44), without the card choosing how to read it.

misleading.why: Acts 14:5 (from memory; check before use) describes Gentiles and Jews together with their leaders planning to mistreat and stone Paul and Barnabas; it does not say 'kill', and it is not the Jews alone.
misleading.fix: A separate line: 'joined Gentiles in a plot to mistreat and stone Paul and Barnabas' (Acts 14:5); keep 'plotted to kill Paul' for Acts 9:23 and 23:12.

misleading.why: 23:12 says 'the Jews formed a conspiracy'; 23:13 (from memory) gives the number as more than forty. The line suggests the whole people.
misleading.fix: 'More than forty Jews bound themselves by oath to kill Paul' (Acts 23:12-13).

misleading.why: 7:1 says 'the Jews there', in Judea, which is the place as well as the people; the line without that reads as all Jews.
misleading.fix: 'The Jews in Judea were trying to kill him' (John 7:1).

misleading.why: A statement of Jesus to a group in dispute (from memory: 'Your accuser is Moses, on whom your hopes are set'), shown as a plain fact in the site's voice. It is also in the Conflict group beside the killing lines.
misleading.fix: Attribute it: 'Jesus tells them their accuser is Moses, in whom they have put their hope' (John 5:45) and file it as Encounters & speech.

misleading.why: Cites a quarrel in which the hearers claim it; the plain statement is better supported elsewhere and would stand without the quarrel.
misleading.fix: Cite Rom 11:1 (Paul, a descendant of Abraham) and Gal 2:15 (Jews by birth) alongside; or word it 'say they are Abraham's descendants' (John 8:33).

misleading.why: Acts 25:2 (from memory) names the chief priests and leaders of the Jews, not the people.
misleading.fix: 'Chief priests and leaders of the Jews asked Festus...' (Acts 25:2-3).

word_pages: The word pages should make plain, without choosing how any book uses it: (1) Hebrew yehudi, Aramaic yehudai and Greek Ioudaios are one family of words built on Judah, and can be translated 'Jew' or 'Judean'; the Berean text uses 'Jew' almost throughout, and that is a translation choice, not the only reading. (2) The word is used by Jews of themselves (Acts 21:39; 22:3; Gal 2:15), by others of Jews (John 4:9; Esth 3:6) and as a title (Matt 2:2; 27:11; John 19:21), and the uses run from favourable to hostile. (3) The Hebrew Bible mostly says Israel, the children of Israel and Judah; 'Jew' as a name is late in it (2 Kings, Jeremiah, Ezra-Nehemiah, Esther, Zech 8:23), with Esther holding 52 of the 69 Hebrew verses. (4) In Greek the word is concentrated in John (71 verses) and Acts (79), and appears in only 5, 6 and 5 verses in Matthew, Mark and Luke. (5) Where the context ties the word to a place (John 7:1, 'in Judea'), show that connection; do not say whether it means Judeans or Jews. (6) List the uses by who speaks and of whom, so a reader sees the whole spread, positive and negative, before any single verse.
summary: The card tells the truth line by line but opens with the killing, claims a single acting body the text does not show, and leaves out that Jesus, Paul, Esther, Mordecai and Aquila are themselves Jews and that many Jews are said to believe. A description that says who they are first, keeps every conflict verse, and a relations list split by direction and with each hard verse given its addressee would let Jewish and other readers trust it.
